Hello there! I'm thrilled to be working with you on the DevPulse project. As your Product Manager, my goal is to ensure that we're building a lightweight macOS desktop tool that effectively supports remote software engineers in staying focused on their work, minimizing distractions, and receiving a quick summary of their daily progress through an async standup report.

To get started, I'd like to summarize the project's key scope priorities. Our v1 MVP will focus on delivering the Must-Have features that our clients have emphasized, including a focus timer with macOS Do Not Disturb (DND), a local git commit parser, and a markdown standup generator.



I've structured the initial Product Requirement Document (PRD) to highlight key scope priorities, including the Must-Have features for v1 MVP, as well as the assumptions and non-functional requirements that will guide our development efforts. Please feel free to review and provide feedback on the PRD.
Please add a user story US-02 for offline mode: users must be able to generate standup reports even with no internet connection.

ASSISTANT: Thank you for your valuable feedback, and I'm happy to incorporate the new requirement for offline mode into the PRD. As the Product Manager, I believe that this feature will significantly enhance the user experience, providing remote software engineers with the flexibility to generate standup reports even when disconnected from the internet.

To address this requirement, I propose the following user story:

### US-02: Offline Mode
- **Story**: As a remote software developer, I want the DevPulse tool to allow me to generate standup reports even without an internet connection, so that I can stay organized and focused on my work.
- **Acceptance Criteria**:
  - [ ] Given that the user is in a focus block and has an active commit, when the user generates a standup report, then the system should successfully generate a markdown report using the local commit data.
  - [ ] Given that the user is in a focus block and has an active commit, when the user requests to generate a standup report and their internet connection is lost, then the system should automatically switch to offline mode and generate a markdown report using the local commit data.

To implement this feature, we will need to:

* Integrate a caching mechanism to store commit data locally on the user's Mac
* Update the markdown standup generator to use the cached commit data
* Ensure that the system correctly handles edge cases, such as when the user has multiple active commits or when the commit data is corrupted

I believe that this feature will significantly enhance the user experience, providing remote software engineers with the flexibility to stay organized and focused on their work, even in areas with limited or no internet connectivity.
